A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 19-page DeepGate4 paper, including Appendices A.1–A.6. Pages 2–19 have identical extracted text and rendered images; the first-page differences are fully readable.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations and scalability measurements, plus OpenABC-D, logic equivalence checking and SAT-solving results in Appendices A.3–A.6.

after.justification: v3 retains all original empirical results from v1, including the main benchmark evaluations and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.7 and Appendix A.2 retain identical graph partitioning, embedding updates, sparse transformer architecture, structural encoding, training objectives, loss balancing and inference acceleration.

E1.justification: ITC99, EPFL Random Control, OpenABC-D, image-processing scale tests, and downstream logic equivalence checking and SAT-solving tasks are unchanged, including appendix coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within every reported experiment, including Tables 1, 3 and 9–11. The full-batch and partitioned model variants and SAT-solver baseline are retained unchanged.

E3.justification: Dataset splits in Tables 5–7, training settings in Section 4.1, circuit-scale testing procedures, and appendix evaluation protocols and metrics are identical.

E4.justification: Component ablations in Table 4, partition-hyperparameter sensitivity in Table 8, and circuit-scale generalization and resource analyses in Figures 7–8 are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages and standard deviations over the last five training epochs in Section 4.1. Uncertainty reporting and any disclosed repetition information remain identical throughout.

E6.justification: All numerical results, rankings and reported findings are identical. For example, Table 3 retains DeepGate4 overall losses of 3.16 ± 0.076 on ITC99 and 4.43 ± 0.577 on EPFL; appendix results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Graph and cone definitions, receptive-field reasoning, mathematical objectives and task definitions remain identical in Section 3 and Appendix A.2. No theoretical derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and scalability, effectiveness and efficiency claims. The added code-availability sentence does not change those claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of receptive fields, generalization, memory scaling, runtime tradeoffs and hyperparameter sensitivity are unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds an abstract sentence stating that code is available and linking the DeepGate4-ICLR-25 GitHub repository; v1 has no corresponding pointer. Implementation settings remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access information, but not the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: Section 2, the bibliography and positioning relative to prior circuit-learning methods, graph transformers and sub-linear GNNs are identical. No cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one code-availability sentence, and the arXiv version/date text changes. The remaining wording, section organization and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page abstract is reflowed with adjusted spacing to accommodate the repository pointer. All figures, tables and subsequent page layouts are unchanged; pages 2–19 render identically.

improvement.justification: The new repository pointer gives readers an explicit location to seek the implementation, modestly improving reproducibility guidance. Scientific content and evidence are unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability, so the supported gain is limited.
